messages:
lee: Heads up — running into weird behavior in the sample paginate-import app when the server starts returning 429 + Retry-After. Progress halts intermittently and we get duplicate page work after bursts.

toni: Which SDK and sample? Any logs?

lee: js-sdk@2.6, sampleapps/paginate-import. Config: concurrency=10, limiter=token-bucket(500/s), perRouteQuotas enabled. Repro: spike the quota usage on route /v1/complete with a short quota window; server replies 429 with Retry-After=3. App stalls for ~20s and then suddenly replays several pages.

sam: Do we see 429 -> client retry logic re-acquiring tokens and resubmitting pages? Could be retry + limiter refill fanout.

lee: Logs show:
```
DEBUG limiter: tokens remaining 0
DEBUG transport: response 429 id=451 retry-after=3
DEBUG paginator: mark-page-failed id=451 reason=429
DEBUG retry: immediate-reenqueue id=451
// no outgoing requests for 18s
// then many requests in <200ms
```
lee: The sudden fanout == duplicates. Also observed that when perRouteQuotas is enabled the limiter is split across routes, but the client-side refill logic refills the global bucket first then per-route buckets, causing transient imbalance.

rachel: Interesting. Is this Node-only? Python uses leaky-bucket and does a staggered refill by default. Go used a slightly different refill schedule. Looks like node's token-bucket refill is bursty.

toni: Two issues to fix: 1) retry behavior should not immediate-reenqueue into the limiter in a way that races with refill; it should push into a jittered retryQueue honoring in-flight markers. 2) the per-route quota implementation needs to ensure proportional refill, not global-first. Should be perRoute.refill(delta * routeShare).

sam: For parity, update js/go/python to use the same refill semantics: incremental trickle over a smoothing window (smoothRefillMs) and default retryMode="buffered". Node's prior default low-latency "immediate" was causing the fanout. Let's make buffered the default to avoid surprising customer duplicates.

ops-bot: Note: add metrics paginator.duplicate_pages and rate.limiter.refill_spike_count for observability.

lee: Quick local fix: changed retry to push into retryQueue with jittered backoff and set limiter.smoothRefillMs=300. No duplicates after 50k pages in stress test. I'll open a sampleapps PR and add a unit test that asserts idempotent page processing under 429 storms.

toni: Also add handling for Retry-After: the SDK should respect server Retry-After for that route and hold re-enqueue until the header window elapses (or at least bias retry timing). Right now we ignore Retry-After and only rely on exponential backoff.

sam: Good call. Implement route-scoped cooldowns: when a route returns Retry-After, mark routeCooldown[route] = now + retryAfter and make retryQueue delay re-enqueue for that route until cooldown expires (with small jitter). That reduces wasted retries and limiter churn.

rachel: For tests: unit test for route cooldown + buffered retry ensures no duplicates; e2e with throttling proxy to return 429+Retry-After for bursts. Also update SDK parity matrix and SDK README.

lee: Opening PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapps/pull/623 — includes retryQueue, per-route cooldown, smoothRefillMs option (default 300ms), and metrics. Will tag you both.

devex-bot: CI started for PR lee/paginate-retry-buffer #623

sam: Small backwards-compat note: moving default retryMode to "buffered" is a behavioral change. Add a changelog entry and an upgrade guide (explain tradeoffs: lower duplicates vs slightly higher median latency).

toni: Also add a runtime opt to set retryMode at app init so customers can opt into immediate low-latency behavior if they accept dedupe risk. Document in quickstart.

lee: Thx — CI passed on the repro branch, adding unit+e2e now. Will coordinate a patch release after reviews.

devex-bot: CI passed for PR lee/paginate-retry-buffer #623 (unit: 21/21, e2e: 2/2) :white_check_mark:
